result.topic_en: Heavily corrected pencil draft of §20 of Riemann's dissertation: under restrictive conditions two simply connected surfaces T and T' can be mapped onto each other point for point continuously; the n-fold connected surface is cut by n−1 cross-cuts into T*, and boundary values for a function ω are prescribed that jump by constants across the cuts (method behind the mapping theorem).

items.english: If the surfaces T and T' are simply connected, then under restricting conditions it is possible to relate them to each other so that to each point of one there corresponds a point of the other moving continuously with it.
